record.original_question: For stadium-like billiards that contain marginally unstable periodic orbits, can one comprehensively characterize their dynamical and escape properties in terms of the reinjection dynamics of trajectories that leave and later return to the neighborhood of those periodic orbits?

evidence.quote: One source of interest and also difficulty with the stadium is the fact that orbits that leave the bouncing ball region are immediately reinjected back, with an angle that is approximately described using an independent stochastic process [4]. Other reinjection mechanisms are possible, depending on the properties of the curvature of the boundary approaching the end points of the bouncing ball orbits.

Open problem 9. Give a comprehensive characterisation of the dynamical (including escape) properties of marginally unstable periodic orbits in stadium-like billiards in terms of their reinjection dynamics.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $Q\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a planar billiard table whose boundary is piecewise smooth (a "stadium-like" table), and consider the billiard flow inside $Q$ (free motion along straight lines with elastic reflection on $\partial Q$). Suppose that $Q$ admits a one-parameter family $\mathcal{F}$ of marginally unstable periodic orbits (MUPOs): periodic trajectories whose linearized Poincaré map has eigenvalues equal to $1$ but which are not Lyapunov stable, so that nearby trajectories escape from a neighborhood $U$ of $\mathcal{F}$ in phase space at a polynomial (rather than exponential) rate. Let $T_U$ denote the first-return time to $U$ for trajectories that leave $U$ and later return, and let $\Phi:\partial U\to\partial U$ denote the induced reinjection map describing the angle and position with which exiting trajectories return to $U$. The classical example is the Bunimovich stadium, where trajectories leaving the "bouncing-ball" region are reinjected with an angle approximately governed by an independent stochastic process; other reinjection mechanisms arise for different boundary curvatures near the endpoints of the MUPO family.

Problem. Provide a comprehensive characterization of the dynamical properties of marginally unstable periodic orbit families in stadium-like billiards — including the asymptotic decay of correlations, the distribution of Poincaré recurrence times, and the asymptotics of the survival probability when a hole is opened in the table (escape dynamics) — purely in terms of the reinjection map $\Phi$ and the statistics of the return time $T_U$.
artifact.category_tag: billiards and marginally unstable periodic orbits
artifact.status_search_result: Searches return work establishing prevalence of MUPOs in chaotic billiards and partial results on bouncing-ball reinjection in the stadium (e.g., polynomial decay of correlations, KAM-like phase-space structures), but no comprehensive characterization of dynamics and escape for general stadium-like billiards in terms of arbitrary reinjection mechanisms appears to have been given. The problem appears to remain open as posed.

status_evidence.title: Prevalence of marginally unstable periodic orbits in chaotic billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Several billiards have families of marginally unstable periodic orbits embedded in their chaotic regions; zero-volume structures reminiscent of KAM islands.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes prevalence of MUPOs but does not give a comprehensive reinjection-based characterization for stadium-like billiards.

status_evidence.title: Marginally Unstable Periodic Orbits in Semiclassical Mushroom Billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Studies MUPOs in mushroom billiards semiclassically.
status_evidence.claim: Treats specific geometries; general reinjection-based classification remains incomplete.
